name: Playhead
notes:
A polish, stability and performance release. No new features: this build is about things working the way you expect, above all on a TV.

**Finding and switching sources**
- Play picks from more than the fastest answer. It used to start with whatever the first provider returned and never looked again; now it gives the other providers a moment, and everything the search finds later is kept as a fallback.
- Far fewer needless switches. A source is no longer judged "stalling" while plenty of video is already downloaded ahead of you. On TVs with little memory this caused most of the unexplained switches.
- Seeking no longer triggers a switch. Jumping to a new position gets its own waiting time.
- A dead source gives way sooner. If another source already has data, Playhead moves to it after about 10 seconds instead of 25–40.
- "Switch now" no longer takes the OK button. When the buffering panel appears, the highlighted button is the harmless one (Keep waiting or Choose source), so pressing OK to pause can't change the source.
- You can see what is happening. The loading screen says which step it is on (searching, asking peers for the file list, connecting, loading the start with a percentage), which source this is ("Source 2 of 14") and why earlier ones were skipped. The error panel lists every source that was tried.
- If the only source found fails and the search then finds another, playback carries on by itself.

**Player no longer gets stuck**
- A playback error in the middle of a film used to freeze the picture for good. The player now retries from the same position, and if that doesn't help it reconnects or moves to the next source.
- If the player sits on "Buffering…" for 30 seconds while the download is healthy, it reconnects by itself.
- Playback no longer pauses when a system panel (volume, assistant, input switcher) appears over the app.
- Stopping a stuck source can no longer block the next Play.
- Smoother on weak TVs: seeking with the remote lands faster, "back 10 seconds" replays from memory, and the on-screen controls redraw far less often.
- The compatibility player uses much less memory on TVs and low-memory devices.

**TV remote and navigation**
- Back from a title returns to exactly where you were: same row, same poster, same scroll position.
- Holding OK no longer repeats the press (no more starting playback from a held OK, no repeated PIN digits).
- "See all", "Cast & crew" and "Remove from history" are reachable with the remote.
- Episode lists keep focus while you move between an episode and its buttons; episode and season menus open with the first item highlighted.
- After typing a search on TV, focus moves to the results.
- Back while adjusting the seek bar cancels the jump instead of applying it.
- The player's help screen keeps focus inside it; the TV player no longer shows the Fullscreen and external-player buttons, which did nothing there.
- "Start over" stays on screen long enough to reach with the remote.
- On a keyboard, "/" can be typed into text fields again.

**Faster browsing**
- Movies and TV pages load rows as you scroll instead of all at once.
- Search, person pages, History and the studio and network lists show a first page and a "Show more" button.
- Smaller poster images are requested where posters are small.

**Stability**
- "Try again" and "Reset" on the startup error screen work, and a reset keeps a backup copy of your library.
- Reset on Windows and Linux only removes Playhead's own temporary files. Earlier builds emptied the system's shared temporary folder; if you used Reset there, other apps' temporary files may have been removed.
- Quitting can no longer hang.
- Pages that fail to load show the error and a Retry button straight away instead of a spinner for up to 40 seconds.
- Offline, your lists no longer look empty: titles that can't be loaded stay in place.
- Re-watching something no longer clears its "watched" mark, and Up Next no longer jumps to the next season after a network hiccup.
- A TMDB key check now tells a rejected key from "couldn't reach TMDB".
- Network settings say that they apply at the next start, and reject invalid ports and tracker addresses.
- Testing a source in Settings no longer drops your other sources until the next search.
- Recent searches keep what you searched for, not every pause in typing.
- Indexer settings survive a crash or power loss during a save.

**Known gaps**
- Downloads can't be started from the app yet; the Downloads list only shows existing ones.
- On Android, adding online subtitles causes a brief pause once per title.
